RIGHT panel: exact 90-degree RIGHT-FACING SIDE elevation for a horizontal 2.5D side-scrolling game, camera perpendicular to the side and at mid-height. The two views show ONE IDENTICAL character at the SAME SCALE on the SAME horizontal baseline, equal top/bottom extent. Plain light neutral background, no floor perspective, subtle contact shadow only, no scenery. Both full objects fit with generous margins. Small labels FRONT and SIDE only. This is NOT an illustration composition, NOT a hero render, NOT three-quarter, NOT isometric, NOT a top view. There are exactly TWO robots rendered, one per panel. Crisp premium stylized 3D shading with calm studio lighting, true parallel projection. Do not add an action pose, inset, shadow duplicate, camera diagram or measurement line.
Most important instruction: the SIDE camera is a literal mechanical side elevation: forward is RIGHT, vertical is UP, depth projects onto itself. Far-side components overlap the near-side components naturally, do NOT cheat the angle to display hidden parts. Do NOT make objects face the viewer in the SIDE panel. Front-facing panels become edge-on in SIDE. The FRONT camera shows front only, no top and no side panels. Both feet/wheels/front-back projection geometry must agree. Use supplied character sheet as the exact identity reference: preserve the humanoid's white/navy/teal curved shells, small crest, black optical face, amber sensor, near-side curved two-jaw clamp forearm and opposite mechanical hand. Extract and CLEANLY REDRAW just FRONT and TRUE SIDE. Neutral comfortable standing pose, both legs straight enough to establish scale, arms hanging naturally. In SIDE the two shoulders, hips, legs and feet overlap; near-side clamp is still visible hanging at hip. Show only one circular ear/temple module. Chest amber sensor is edge-on, not facing camera. Head, torso and feet ALL point RIGHT. Match the original character proportions without redesigning it.
